value: Which factors shape audience members' perceptions of the authenticity of influencer-produced sponsored content, and can priming with an introductory text and with encouraged or discouraged participation alter those perceptions?

Shows in a 2x2 online experiment that a short positive or negative introductory text before an identical sponsored travel vlog flips viewers' judgements of the vlogger's authenticity, and that encouraging audience participation blunts the negative prime.

quote: The subjects were randomly assigned to a condition to improve the internal validity of the experiment.

The results verified the significance of priming: the same sponsored content can result in opposite reactions among the audience members depending on the positive/negative valence of the introductory text attached, highlighting the central importance of strategic communication related to the perception of sponsored content.
This study explores how positive and negative priming of sponsored content shapes the authenticity perception of the vlogger among its audience members.

value: Attaching an introductory text of opposite valence to the identical sponsored vlog produced opposite authenticity perceptions of the vlogger, supporting both the positive- and negative-priming hypotheses.
quote: Overall, the results confirmed that priming was strongly associated with the authenticity perception of the vlog viewers in both the positive and negative priming circumstances, confirming H1a and H1b.

value: Encouraging versus discouraging audience participation changed authenticity perception only when the introductory text was negative, not when it was positive.
quote: Based on these results, the manipulation of participation had a significant effect on the perception of authenticity only in the negative introduction text conditions.

value: Negative priming did not spill over onto the endorsed products: negative attitudes towards the products did not differ across the manipulation groups.
quote: Though no differences were found in the negative manipulations, it can be concluded that the manipulation did not influence the perception of the endorsed products.

value: Positive priming shifted perceptions of the vlogger, the video and the product, whereas negative priming moved only perceptions of the vlogger.
quote: The findings also showed that positive priming influences both the vlogger’s authenticity as well as attitudes towards the endorsed video and product, while the effect of negative priming was restricted to only the vlogger.

value: Because negativity concentrates on the influencer rather than on the sponsor, sponsored content carries less reputational risk for the organization than for the vlogger.
quote: The results suggest that sponsored content is less risky for organizations than influencers: the vloggers will receive a much greater share of negativity when content is perceived as inauthentic.
